mission.title: cilium: L2Announcement with externalTrafficPolicy: Local
mission.description: L2Announcement with externalTrafficPolicy: Local. This issue affects 27+ users.

steps.title: Identify cilium troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your cilium deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n cilium -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cilium
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cilium -n cilium --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cilium -n cilium --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n cilium --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.

resolution.summary:
Hmm. So the L2Announcement feature doesn't "implement" `externalTrafficPolicy` as in, we ignore the setting at the present. That means that we might announce the IP from a node that doesn't have a pod for the service, thus violating the wish expressed with `externalTrafficPolicy`. 

The feature relies on the generic service LB functionality to forward traffic received for a given IP.
